Let

\[
I_n=\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{\sin(x/n)}{x^2+x}\,dx.
\]

The singularity at \(x=0\) is removable since \(\sin(x/n)/(x^2+x)\sim 1/n\).

Make the change of variables \(x=nt\), so \(dx=n\,dt\). Then

\[
I_n=\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{\sin t}{t(1+nt)}\,dt.
\]

Now estimate the absolute value:

\[
|I_n|
\le \int_{0}^{1}\frac{|\sin t|}{t(1+nt)}\,dt
+\int_{1}^{\infty}\frac{|\sin t|}{t(1+nt)}\,dt.
\]

For \(0<t\le 1\), \(|\sin t|/t\le 1\), so

\[
\int_{0}^{1}\frac{|\sin t|}{t(1+nt)}\,dt
\le \int_{0}^{1}\frac{dt}{1+nt}
=\frac{1}{n}\ln(1+n).
\]

For \(t\ge 1\), \(|\sin t|\le 1\) and \(1+nt\ge nt\), so

\[
\int_{1}^{\infty}\frac{|\sin t|}{t(1+nt)}\,dt
\le \int_{1}^{\infty}\frac{dt}{n t^2}
=\frac{1}{n}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
|I_n|\le \frac{\ln(1+n)+1}{n}\to 0
\qquad (n\to\infty).
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
